newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-ELS HEADS BEST FIELD YET FOR SOUTH AFRICAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS HEADS BEST FIELD YET FOR SOUTH AFRICAN OPEN.

text.p: Defending champion and world number four Ernie Els of South Africa heads a strong field for the South African Open starting on Thursday at Glendower Golf Club.

While Els looks for his third South African Open title after wins in 1992 and last year, he faces tough opposition from the likes of world number 12 Nick Price of Zimbabwe, world-ranked 17 Mark McNulty, also of Zimbabwe, Welshman Ian Woosnam, Fijian Vijay Singh and Italy's Costantino Rocca.
This year's Open, the first co-operative event between the Southern African and the European tours, has attracted the best field in the history of the championship.

The cream of South African golf is taking part, including United States-based players David Frost and Fulton Allem, while some top performers in Europe have made the trip across the Indian Ocean from Australia - albeit with the notable exceptions of Nick Faldo, Colin Montgomerie, Bernhard Langer and Sam Torrance.
Significantly, nearly all of the expected front-runners in the South African Open this week have arrived at Glendower in good form.

Els returns to his home country fresh from a one-shot victory in the Johnnie Walker Classic at Australia's Hope Island resort and a closing 65 on Sunday for a share of eighth place in the Heineken Classic in Perth.
Price, after a 1996 plagued with sinus trouble, is moving back up the rankings after a third-place finish in the Phoenix Open two weeks ago.
McNulty, apart from a slight wobble in Durban's players championship last week, has produced some of the best golf of his career to win three of the last four events on the Southern African tour.

Emerging Irish star Padraig Harrington finished one shot behind Els on Sunday in the Heineken Classic after a course record 63 in the second round and the French duo of Marc Farry and Jean van de Velde played consistent golf in the same tournament to share third place behind winner Miguel Angel Martin of Spain.
After Glendower, the golfers remain in South Africa for the next two events on the European tour - a pro-am at Sun City and the South African PGA at Houghton.
